=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller SPA Positions (SPA-N-001 to SPA-N-016)

**Preliminary point:** I have not treated any clause as [STANDARD] or closed. The Seller's labels, its "FINAL / not to be re-opened" statement, and its market-practice assertions are the Seller's characterisation, not agreed terms. Several "[STANDARD]" items (buyer knowledge, time limits, Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay) are substantively adverse to the Buyer. The "10-20% cap / 1% basket / 12-18 month" market claims are unsupported, and NSW counsel should verify them against comparable deals.

**Priority items:**
1. **Privacy incident (SPA-N-012):** Under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth), an eligible data breach assessment must be completed within 30 days of reasonable grounds to suspect one. The disclosure is dated 22 September 2026 and today is 5 November 2026, so this may already be overdue. Confirm status immediately.
2. **Bluefen consent (SPA-N-008):** About 30% of revenue depends on it.
3. **Riverlark (SPA-N-009) and bonuses (SPA-N-010):** These are price-mechanics issues, not indemnity issues, under the debt-free/cash-free basis.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller position:** Aggregate general Warranty Claims capped at 20% of price (AUD 4.8m).
- **Buyer wants:** A higher cap (I'd open at 30-40% of price, around AUD 7.2m-9.6m, to be validated against market), with fundamental warranties, tax, fraud and specific indemnities carved out.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at a higher general cap with carve-outs. The 20% cap is also the main limit on recovery for known issues, so it matters more because of the disclosure package.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
- **Seller position:** AUD 25k de minimis; AUD 250k deductible basket (about 1.04% of price). Only the excess over the basket is recoverable.
- **Buyer wants:** A lower de minimis (around AUD 10k, or aggregated claims of a related series), and a **tipping** basket so that once it is exceeded, recovery runs from the first dollar. Thresholds should not apply to fundamental, tax or specific indemnity claims.
- **Recommendation:** Tipping basket with a lower de minimis, because a deductible basket of AUD 250k absorbs much of the realistic exposure before the Buyer recovers anything.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller position:** General claims must be notified within 18 months. Any limitation applies to all claims.
- **Buyer wants:** 24-36 months for general warranties, a longer period for tax (the ATO amendment period is generally four years, so tax claims should run to the end of the statute period plus a buffer), and 6 years for fundamental warranties (the Limitation Act 1969 (NSW) contract period).
- **Recommendation:** Reject the "applies to all Claims" wording. Each category needs its own period, because a single 18-month period would expire before many SaaS tax and IP issues surface.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller position:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties.
- **Buyer wants:** Fundamental warranties (capacity, authority, title to shares, capitalisation) capped at the full purchase price, with a 6-year claim period, outside the basket and de minimis.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Title is the core asset being bought, and applying a general cap to it leaves the Buyer exposed for the whole purchase price.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller position:** Not addressed. The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to "all Claims of any nature". No fraud carve-out appears.
- **Buyer wants:** An express carve-out so that limitations, caps, time bars and non-reliance do not protect the Seller for fraud, dishonesty or wilful concealment, including in the disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** Insert the carve-out. Without it, the Seller's limitation package would apply to fraud, which is unacceptable for a deal of this size.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller position:** General disclosure of the entire data room (up to 5pm 22 September 2026), the Accounts and public registers, "without limiting" specific disclosures (Schedule 7; DL 1.1-1.2).
- **Buyer wants:** Specific, fair disclosure only. Data room and public registers should not be disclosed generally. Disclosure should be against specific warranties, and should not qualify the specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** Reject general data room disclosure. Read together with the buyer-knowledge clause (SPA-N-007), it would disclose everything in the data room and then bar claims about it.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller position:** No claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, including matters discoverable from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** An express "pro-sandbagging" clause, so that the Buyer can claim regardless of its knowledge, with specific indemnities covering known matters. Under NSW law, the effect of knowledge on damages is not settled, so the position should be stated expressly.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. The Buyer has identified known issues (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, privacy, bonuses), so a knowledge bar would remove recovery for exactly the risks the Buyer is concerned about. Address these through specific indemnities and price.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller position:** Seller will use reasonable endeavours. Consent treated as satisfied when the counterparty's written consent is delivered.
- **Buyer wants:** Final, unconditional written Bluefen consent (or evidence the DD-002 cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied) as a condition precedent to Completion, with the Buyer able to walk away if it is not obtained. Consent should cover the share sale expressly. Any consent costs or conditions borne by the Seller.
- **Recommendation:** Make it a true CP. The Disclosure Letter confirms no final consent exists, and "reasonable endeavours" gives the Buyer no protection on ~30% of revenue.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller position:** Approximately AUD 3.2m outstanding; a release to be provided after Completion.
- **Buyer wants:** Full repayment at Completion from the Seller's proceeds (debt-free basis), with a payoff letter and an executed security discharge (PPSR) delivered at Completion. Any shortfall is deducted from the price.
- **Recommendation:** Reject post-Completion release. On a debt-free basis, the Seller should discharge the debt out of the funds flow; leaving it open exposes the Buyer to the lender.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller position:** AUD 420k conditional Completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not in the funds flow.
- **Buyer wants:** The AUD 420k, plus employer on-costs (NSW payroll tax, superannuation, and any other on-costs), treated as debt-like items deducted from price, or paid by the Seller at or before Completion. Confirm whether any bonuses are triggered by the transaction itself.
- **Recommendation:** Treat as a price deduction. Completion bonuses are a Company liability that the Buyer would otherwise inherit, and they are missing from the funds flow.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller position:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; considered adequate.
- **Buyer wants:** A specific indemnity covering all Ironquay claims, including ownership of Project Materials, third-party IP claims and the AUD 180k open balance. Transfer of SOW3 materials conditional on payment (DD-004 cl 7.3) must be resolved, with a confirmatory assignment and written evidence of payment (or payment by the Seller) as a CP. Indemnity should sit outside the cap.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. The Seller's own disclosure confirms no payment receipt or assignment exists, so the SOW3 payment alone does not protect the Buyer's title to the materials.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller position:** Not expected to be material. Disclosure says the investigation is preliminary and no loss amount is stated.
- **Buyer wants:** A forensic investigation (independent) before Completion. Confirmation of whether an eligible data breach has occurred and whether notification was made (OAIC and affected individuals). A specific indemnity for all costs, regulatory action and third-party claims, outside the cap and basket, with a longer claim period. Specific privacy warranties.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the "not material" characterisation. About 1,240 records of personal information are involved, and the 30-day assessment window may already have passed.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller position:** Three renewals totalling AUD 330k are ordinary course operating costs.
- **Buyer wants:** Copies of the contracts, term, termination rights and change-of-control provisions. Confirmation of whether any pre-Completion portion is accrued, and that the Seller bears any cost tied to pre-Completion periods. Above-market or non-cancellable terms treated as debt-like, or subject to a pricing adjustment.
- **Recommendation:** Verify before accepting "ordinary course." The disclosure states the documents do not show whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable or accrued.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller position:** A single regime for all claims (general warranty, fundamental, tax, IP, specific).
- **Buyer wants:** Separate regimes: (a) general warranties (capped, thresholds, 24-36 months); (b) fundamental warranties (full price, 6 years, no thresholds); (c) tax (indemnity, statute period, no thresholds); (d) specific indemnities (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses, privacy, Sandbar, lease, Mossvale); (e) fraud (uncapped).
- **Recommendation:** Reject the uniform regime. A single cap and time limit across these categories would undercut the protection the Buyer is seeking for each.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller position:** Title evidenced by the share register (DD-012), which records Harbourglass as holder of 100%. The disclosure does not confirm Buyer verification.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent verification: current ASIC company extract, inspection of the original register and share certificates, a PPSR search over the shares, confirmation of no options or other issued equity, and a chain-of-title check. Title warranty, plus delivery of the transfer and register updates at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Complete these checks before signing. A register extract is the Seller's source document, not independent verification.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller position:** Tax and IP warranties "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** A pre-Completion tax indemnity (outside cap and basket, to the statute period plus buffer). Tax due diligence on pre-Completion periods, including SaaS GST treatment and payroll tax. IP warranties (ownership of core platform IP, non-infringement, open-source compliance, contractor IP assignments), with IP claims outside the general cap given the Ironquay issue.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. The general regime is capped and time-limited, and tax and IP are exactly where SaaS businesses carry latent exposure.

---

### Items not in the 16 but flagged in the Seller package
- **Office lease (DD-007):** Confirm whether landlord consent is required for the share sale.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** Confirm whether the assignment restriction is triggered by a change of control.

**Caveat:** This is a commercial review to support the deal team. Final drafting, CP mechanics, and NSW-specific points (including whether the Civil Liability Act 2002 (NSW) proportionate liability provisions should be excluded for warranty claims) should be confirmed by NSW counsel.
